hints.en: Without a format: `pd.to_datetime(sample)`. With one: `pd.to_datetime(sample, format="%d.%m.%Y")`. Use `.dt.month.tolist()` on both.

hints.tr: Saat de varsa biçime eklenir: `"%d.%m.%Y %H:%M"`. Büyük `%H` saat, büyük `%M` dakika.
hints.en: If there is a time, add it to the format: `"%d.%m.%Y %H:%M"`. Upper-case `%H` is the hour, upper-case `%M` the minute.

hints.tr:
Çözüm:

```python
import pandas as pd

sample = pd.Series(["09.03.2024", "10.03.2024", "11.03.2024"])

print(pd.to_datetime(sample).dt.month.tolist())
print(pd.to_datetime(sample, format="%d.%m.%Y").dt.month.tolist())

orders = pd.read_csv("orders.csv")
ordered = pd.to_datetime(orders["ordered_at"], format="%d.%m.%Y %H:%M")

print(ordered.min(), ordered.max())
print(ordered.dt.month.value_counts().sort_index().to_dict())
```
hints.en:
The solution:

```python
import pandas as pd

sample = pd.Series(["09.03.2024", "10.03.2024", "11.03.2024"])

print(pd.to_datetime(sample).dt.month.tolist())
print(pd.to_datetime(sample, format="%d.%m.%Y").dt.month.tolist())

orders = pd.read_csv("orders.csv")
ordered = pd.to_datetime(orders["ordered_at"], format="%d.%m.%Y %H:%M")

print(ordered.min(), ordered.max())
print(ordered.dt.month.value_counts().sort_index().to_dict())
```
